## What "covered" means here

A technique counts as covered when at least one stack product satisfies a NIST 800-53 R5 control that the [CTID NIST 800-53 R5 mapping](https://github.com/center-for-threat-informed-defense/attack-control-framework-mappings) links to it ([`data/vendor_to_technique.jsonl`](/data/vendor_to_technique.jsonl), the `vendor_to_control` x `control_to_technique` join). This measures control-mapping availability, not a tested detection or prevention. Mappings that CTID keyed on an ATT&CK id that v19 revoked are carried forward to the live successor through [`superseded_by.jsonl`](/data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl) (520 of 17,668 edge rows are keyed on a revoked id), so revoked ids are never counted as techniques.

Products listed under two keys in the edge table are counted once: `cyberark` -> `cyberark-pam`; `elastic-siem` -> `elastic-security`; `microsoft-defender-for-o365` -> `microsoft-defender-for-office-365`; `qualys` -> `qualys-vmdr`; `rapid7` -> `rapid7-insightvm`; `splunk-es` -> `splunk-enterprise-security`; `tenable` -> `tenable-io`.

Overall: 462 of the 697 live Enterprise v19.2 techniques and sub-techniques are covered (66.3%); 235 are not.

To recompute: `python scripts/compute_coverage.py` (writes all four files in `scores/`; `--check` exits non-zero if they are stale).

## Why the gaps are where they are

Coverage is derived through NIST controls, so a gap means no stack product satisfies any control mapped to the technique. Of the 235 uncovered techniques, 231 have no CTID NIST 800-53 mapping at all (under their own id or a revoked predecessor), so no product can be credited for them through this join, whatever it actually does. Distribution of mapped controls across the gaps: 0 controls: 231, 1 control: 4.

The gap list is therefore ranked by adversary use rather than by NIST depth (`group_count desc, software_count desc, campaign_count desc, nist_control_depth desc, technique_id`). Priority basis: group_count (the number of ATT&CK groups documented using the technique, from the v19.2 profiles): critical >= 20, high >= 10, medium >= 3, low otherwise. Gaps by priority: critical 22, high 23, medium 66, low 124.

## Recommended capability additions

The capabilities, example vendors and key technique families are editorial; the coverage figures are computed on each run.

| Capability | Example vendors | Tactic coverage today | Key families with uncovered members |

| DLP / CASB | Netskope, Microsoft Purview, Forcepoint | Collection 65.9%; Exfiltration 94.7% | T1213 (1/7), T1560 (2/4), T1074 (3/3) |
| UEBA (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) | Microsoft Sentinel Analytics, Splunk UBA, Securonix | Discovery 30.6%; Credential Access 94.0%; Lateral Movement 95.7% | T1082 (1/1), T1083 (1/1), T1087 (1/5) |
| Endpoint Hardening / Application Control | CrowdStrike App Control, Carbon Black App Control, Tanium | Stealth 69.6%; Defense Impairment 78.6%; Execution 85.9% | T1027 (9/19) |
| NDR (Network Detection & Response) | Corelight, Darktrace, ExtraHop Reveal(x) | Command and Control 86.7%; Lateral Movement 95.7% | none |

Family figures are uncovered/total techniques in the family (the technique and its sub-techniques).

## How to use this analysis

1. Load the [TeamStarWolf Navigator layers](/navigator/) to see coverage on the matrix.
2. Run `python scripts/compute_coverage.py` after the edge tables change; it rewrites this page and the three JSON files.
3. Treat a gap here as "no mapped control in the stack", then confirm with real detection tests before building a business case.
4. As products are added to `data/vendor_to_control.jsonl`, rebuild the join with `python scripts/build_ctid_edges.py` and re-run this script.
5. Cross-reference [CONTROLS_MAPPING.md](/CONTROLS_MAPPING.md) to see which NIST controls a candidate product would satisfy.
